origin.why_angular: long used only for inscribing names and brief memorials upon wood or stone, which is what their angular shapes are owed to
origin.spread: the older and simpler form spread eastward in the Second Age to Men, Dwarves and Orcs, each altering them; one such simple form was still used by the Men of Dale and a similar one by the Rohirrim
origin.cite: LotR App E II, The Cirth

daeron.name: the Angerthas Daeron
daeron.who: attributed in Elvish tradition to Daeron, minstrel and loremaster of King Thingol of Doriath
daeron.note: the richest and most ordered form of the Cirth. The principal additions -- the series 13-17 and 23-28 -- were most probably inventions of the Noldor of Eregion, being for sounds not found in Sindarin.
daeron.cite: LotR App E II, The Cirth

moria.name: the Angerthas Moria
moria.who: the Dwarves of Moria, from Eregion
moria.note: the Long Rune-rows of Moria. The Dwarves introduced unsystematic changes in value and certain new cirth. This arrangement is the one in the tomb-inscription.
moria.cite: LotR App E II, The Cirth

erebor.name: the mode of Erebor
erebor.note: a further modification of the Angerthas Moria, exemplified in the Book of Mazarbul. Appendix E's own table excludes these peculiarities except for the Ereborian cirth 57 and 58.

refused.why: Appendix E describes the CONCEPT -- older modes in which only the consonants were denoted by full letters -- and never states which tengwa carries which Sindarin vowel. Those values are in the West-gate specimen and the mode figure, which are pictures. The text was searched and does not carry them.
refused.what_would_answer: a measurement of the West-gate inscription made by this archive's own instrument, as the centreline sheets measure Christopher Tolkien's linework -- not a reading of someone else's transcription.

refused.what: a CITATION for the ~29 certh Appendix E's prose does not name
refused.why: Appendix E's Table of Values is a FIGURE. The archive holds those values as [I-H], read off the plate and marked as such in their own notes; what they lack is a citation, not a value.
refused.what_would_answer: a prose witness for each. The three rearrangement principles do not supply one: they say what a shape MEANS given a base certh, not which certh is the base.

refused.why: the archive draws its own 60 cirth as SVG and needs no font to SHOW them -- that refusal was withdrawn as simply false. What a font would add is text a reader can SELECT, COPY and search, which an SVG cannot give.
refused.what_would_answer: a Cirth face whose licence is read from the file itself, recorded in arda_assets.json with its hand, as the two tengwar faces are.

note: Built from what Appendix E STATES IN PROSE. Its Table of Values is a figure and is not reproduced or reconstructed; the ~40 cirth it draws and does not name are absent, and `refused` says so with what would answer each. Every value here carries its own citation.
